subject: Biology
title: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes
summary: Modern biotechnology rests on genetic engineering (changing DNA/RNA, introducing it into hosts) and bioprocess engineering (sterile large-scale culture). The first recombinant DNA was made by Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer (1972) by linking an antibiotic-resistance gene to a native plasmid of Salmonella typhimurium.
Tools: restriction enzymes (molecular scissors), DNA ligase (glue), cloning vectors (plasmids, phages), competent hosts and gel electrophoresis.
Process: isolate DNA → cut with restriction enzyme → amplify with PCR → ligate into vector → transform host → select recombinants → grow in bioreactors → downstream processing.

formulas.name: Restriction enzymes
formulas.formula: first discovered: Hind II (cuts at a specific 6-bp sequence);  exonucleases remove nucleotides from ends; endonucleases cut inside;  recognise palindromic sequences

formulas.name: Naming EcoRI
formulas.formula: E = Escherichia (genus), co = coli (species), R = RY13 (strain), I = first enzyme isolated from that strain

formulas.name: Palindrome and sticky ends
formulas.formula: 5′-GAATTC-3′ / 3′-CTTAAG-5′ reads the same 5′→3′ on both strands;  EcoRI cuts between G and A → sticky ends that pair with complementary ends

formulas.name: Gel electrophoresis
formulas.formula: DNA (negatively charged) moves towards the anode through agarose gel (from seaweed);  smaller fragments move farther;  stained with ethidium bromide, seen as orange bands under UV;  bands cut out and purified (elution)

formulas.name: Cloning vector features
formulas.formula: origin of replication (ori — controls copy number);  selectable marker (ampicillin, chloramphenicol, tetracycline or kanamycin resistance);  cloning (recognition) sites, preferably single;  small size

formulas.name: pBR322
formulas.formula: ori + rop (proteins for replication) + amp^R + tet^R;  BamHI site in tet^R; PstI and PvuI in amp^R

formulas.name: Insertional inactivation
formulas.formula: insert in tet^R gene → recombinants lose tetracycline resistance;  β-galactosidase (lacZ) insertion → recombinants give colourless colonies, non-recombinants blue (with chromogenic substrate)

formulas.name: Vectors for plants and animals
formulas.formula: Agrobacterium tumefaciens — Ti plasmid (tumour-inducing; disarmed for gene transfer);  retroviruses disarmed for animal cells

formulas.name: Making cells competent
formulas.formula: divalent cations (Ca²⁺) → heat shock (ice, 42 °C, ice) → plasmid enters;  other methods: microinjection (animal nucleus), biolistics/gene gun (plant cells, gold or tungsten particles), disarmed pathogen vectors

formulas.name: PCR steps
formulas.formula: denaturation (~94 °C) → annealing of primers → extension by Taq polymerase (from Thermus aquaticus, thermostable);  copies double each cycle (2ⁿ)

formulas.name: Isolating DNA
formulas.formula: lyse cells with lysozyme (bacteria), cellulase (plants), chitinase (fungi);  remove RNA with ribonuclease, proteins with protease;  chilled ethanol precipitates DNA (fine threads)

formulas.name: Bioreactors
formulas.formula: large vessels (100–1000 L) giving optimum temperature, pH, O₂, substrate;  stirred-tank (agitator, oxygen delivery, foam control, temperature and pH control, sampling ports)

formulas.name: Downstream processing
formulas.formula: separation and purification of the product, formulation with preservatives, clinical trials for drugs, quality control

examples.title: Fragments from a circular plasmid
examples.problem: A circular plasmid has four EcoRI sites. How many fragments form after complete digestion?
examples.solution: In a circular DNA, n cuts give n fragments: 4 fragments. (A linear DNA with n cuts gives n + 1.)

examples.title: Blue–white screening
examples.problem: On a plate with X-gal, which colonies carry recombinant plasmids?
examples.solution: Colourless (white) colonies — the insert disrupts lacZ (insertional inactivation), so no β-galactosidase forms to give the blue colour.

examples.title: Why one recognition site?
examples.problem: Why should a vector have only one site for the chosen restriction enzyme?
examples.solution: More than one site would cut the vector into several pieces, complicating gene cloning.

examples.title: Taq polymerase
examples.problem: Why is Taq polymerase used in PCR?
examples.solution: It comes from the thermophilic bacterium Thermus aquaticus and stays active during the high-temperature denaturation step, so fresh enzyme isn't needed each cycle.

examples.title: Agrobacterium
examples.problem: Why is Agrobacterium called a natural genetic engineer of plants?
examples.solution: It naturally transfers a piece of its Ti plasmid DNA (T-DNA) into plant cells, transforming them into tumour cells; a disarmed Ti plasmid can deliver useful genes instead.

examples.title: Copies after PCR cycles
examples.problem: Starting with one DNA molecule, how many copies after 10 PCR cycles?

topics.title: Definition of biotechnology
topics.explain: The European Federation of Biotechnology (EFB) defines it as the integration of natural science and organisms, cells, parts thereof and molecular analogues for products and services.

topics.title: Basic steps in genetic engineering
topics.explain: Identify DNA with desirable genes; introduce it into the host; maintain the introduced DNA in the host and transfer it to progeny. Plasmid DNA acts as a vector to carry the foreign DNA.

topics.title: DNA ligase
topics.explain: Joins cut DNA fragments having the same kind of sticky ends; the same restriction enzyme must be used to cut both the vector and the source DNA.

topics.title: Recombinant DNA expression
topics.explain: The cloned gene is expressed under suitable conditions to make recombinant protein in a host. Small-volume cultures can't make large quantities, so continuous culture systems keep cells in their physiologically most active log/exponential phase.

topics.title: Selection with antibiotics
topics.explain: Transformants are grown on media with antibiotics; only cells carrying the plasmid (with resistance gene) survive. Replica plating on a second antibiotic reveals insertional inactivation.

topics.title: Alternative selectable markers
topics.explain: Selection with two antibiotics is cumbersome, so chromogenic substrates (blue–white) are used as an easier method.
